info.title: chess runner
info.description: Builds, tests and analyses engine variants. Every command of the `chess` CLI maps onto one of these routes.

post.summary: Searches a position to a limit (depth 20 when none is given) and answers with the best move and lines.
Starts a live search, replacing any other. Reports arrive as `analysis.info` events until it is stopped.
Queues several experiments under one name. They run in order.

get.summary: The Reckless checkout's branches and upstream's, most recently committed first: what can be built or tested.

post.summary: Queues a build. A commit that is already built finishes at once with the existing build.

get.summary:
Live events as server-sent events: every event has an id, and reconnecting with the last id seen replays what was
missed.

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: Replay events after this id. `Last-Event-ID` does the same for a reconnecting browser.

parameters.name: batch
parameters.description: Only the experiments of this batch.

post.summary:
Queues an experiment: a dev ref against a base ref, through the default funnel for its kind, the given stages,
or a single match (`preset`).

delete.summary: Cancels a queued experiment or stops a running one.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: How many jobs, newest first. Default 50.

delete.summary: Cancels a queued job or stops a running one.

get.summary: A job's output so far, as plain text.

The bot: whether a token is stored and whose it is, whether it is online and how its connection stands, the
matches of the games it is playing, and its settings. The token itself is never returned.
The bots online on Lichess now (up to fifty), with their ratings: who there is to challenge.

post.summary:
Challenges a Lichess player (usually another bot) to a standard game with our build. If accepted, the game starts
like any other and is recorded as a match. 409 while the bot is offline.

Looks for a game: the bot challenges a random online bot near its rating, at a clock from `seek_clocks`, and tries
another when one declines or does not answer within 25 seconds. Answers the status, whose `seek` follows the
search. 409 while the bot is offline or has no token.

delete.summary: Stops looking for games and withdraws the challenge waiting for an answer. Games in progress are played out.

get.summary: The bot's settings: the build that plays, its hash, threads and move overhead, and which challenges it accepts.

put.summary:
Replaces the bot's settings (fields left out take their defaults) and answers with them as stored, numbers brought
into range. 400 if the build does not exist or a range is upside down.

post.summary:
Takes the bot online: it follows the account's event stream, answers challenges by its settings and plays every
game that starts, and stays online across restarts until stopped. 409 without a token, a BOT account or a build.
Takes the bot offline. Games in progress are played out.

put.summary:
Stores the bot's Lichess token, once Lichess has accepted it, and answers with the account it belongs to (whose
`bot` says whether it can play yet). The token stays in the runner's data directory and is never returned. 400 if
Lichess rejects it.

delete.summary: Forgets the token and takes the bot offline. Games in progress are played out.

post.summary:
Turns the token's account into a Lichess BOT account. IRREVERSIBLE: a BOT account can never play as a person
again, and Lichess only upgrades an account that has never played a game. Requires `{ "confirm": true }`.

get.summary:
Recent matches, newest first, without their moves: local ones and the bot's Lichess games alike, unless `source`
picks one kind.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: How many matches, newest first. Default 50.

parameters.name: source
parameters.description: Only local matches (`local`) or only the bot's Lichess games (`lichess`). Both when absent.

oneOf.description: Which matches a list holds.

post.summary:
Starts a match between two builds and returns it. The moves arrive as `match.move` events, the thinking engine's
progress as `match.info`, and the end as `match.ended`. One local match runs at a time: 409 while another is
running. The bot's Lichess games run beside it and do not count.

get.summary:
A match with its headers, every move (evaluation, depth, nodes, time and the clocks after it), the clocks now, the
side to move, its status and, once over, the result and reason.

delete.summary:
Stops the running match, which is recorded as aborted, and returns it. 409 if it is not running. A Lichess game is
resigned instead (aborted, if it has not got going), and the answer is the game as it stands: it ends, and
`match.ended` follows, once Lichess confirms.

get.summary: The match as PGN, with a comment on every move (score/depth, time, nodes, clock) like the test PGNs.
The runner's version, machine and engine checkout.
One game as PGN, with each move's evaluation, depth, nodes and time in its comment.

Account.description: The Lichess account the token belongs to.

bot.description: Whether it is a BOT account, the only kind the Bot API plays with.

id.description: The lower-case id, as games name players.

build.description: The build to analyse with. Defaults to the newest build.

fen.description: The position as FEN, or `startpos` (the default).

limits.description: Where a one-shot search stops. Left empty, a one-shot search stops at depth 20; a live one runs until stopped.

moves.description: Moves from that position, in UCI notation.

multipv.description: How many best lines to report.

lines.description: The last report of each line, best first.

BotState.description: Where the bot's connection to Lichess stands.

Branch.description: A branch of the checkout, newest commit first.

bench.description: The node count the commit message claims (`Bench: N`).

date.description: When its commit was made, ISO 8601.

name.description: The name to build or test, such as `main` or `upstream/main`.

bench.description: Nodes searched by `bench`: the functional fingerprint.

bench_expected.description: The `Bench:` line of the commit message, when it has one. A build whose bench differs from it is suspect.

network.description: The network file the build embeds.

nps.description: Nodes per second during `bench` on this machine.

ref.description: The ref that was asked for, such as a branch name.
A branch, tag or commit of the Reckless checkout, such as `main` or `upstream/main`.

clock_seconds.description: The initial clock in seconds. Lichess takes 0, 15, 30, 45, 60, 90, or a whole number of minutes.

color.description: The colour our build plays. Default random.

username.description: Who to challenge: a Lichess username, usually another bot's.

id.description: The challenge id, which becomes the game id if it is accepted.

Estimate.description: Elo and normalized Elo with 95% intervals (`±`), from game pairs.

batch.description: The batch it was submitted with, if any.

current.description: The stage running now, while running.

results.description: Results of the stages run so far, in order.

tests.description: Its matches, in the order they ran.

GameResult.description: How a game came out, as PGN writes it.

index.description: Position in the match's PGN, from 0.

Info.description: One `info` line with a principal variation.

pv.description: The principal variation in UCI notation (`e2e4`).

result.description: What the job produced, such as `{ "build": 3 }`.

oneOf.description: Build a commit of the Reckless checkout and bench it.
Run an experiment's funnel.

Kind.description: What kind of change an experiment tests, which picks its funnel.

LichessGame.description: What a game played on Lichess adds to the record.

id.description: The Lichess game id, such as `q7ZvsdUF`.

speed.description: `bullet`, `blitz`, `rapid` or `classical`, as Lichess names the game's speed.

oneOf.description: The account the token belongs to, once Lichess has said.

error.description: What went wrong last, while `state` is `error`.

online.description: Whether the bot is switched on. It stays on across restarts until stopped.

playing.description: The matches of the games being played now.

seek.description:
Whether the bot is looking for games by challenging other bots, the challenge it is waiting on, and how the
search last went.

session.description: Events of this search carry this id.

Machine.description: The machine the runner is on, read once at start.

book.description: Whether the opening came from the book.

clock_white_ms.description: What each clock holds now, the thinking side's counting down. Absent when the match has no clock.

oneOf.description:
Set when the bot played the game on Lichess. Its clocks are Lichess's, and the opponent's moves carry no
evaluation.

minimal.description: Whether the engines ran with `Minimal` on, and so reported nothing while thinking.

oneOf.description: Why the game ended, once it has.

start_fen.description: The position the game started from: `startpos` or a FEN. Any opening moves are already played in it.

MatchMove.description: One move of a game, with what the engine that played it reported.

clock_white_ms.description: What each clock holds after the move, increment included. Absent when the match has no clock.

oneOf.description: The mover's last score, from the mover's side.

ply.description: 1 for the first move of the game.

black.description: The build that plays Black, by id.

hash.description: Hash table size in MiB for each engine. Default 16, as in the tests.

minimal.description:
End decided games early, as the tests do: a side that has scored -4 or worse for three moves loses, and a
level game drawn from move 30. Off by default, so the game is played out.
Reckless's `Minimal` option, which the tests set: the engine then reports only its final line, so there is nothing
to watch while it thinks. Off by default, so `match.info` events flow; it does not change how the engine plays.

threads.description: Search threads for each engine. Default 1, so a match uses two threads and can run beside a test.

white.description: The build that plays White, by id.

MatchSpec.description: One match between the dev and base builds.

oneOf.description: Stop when the SPRT decides. Without one, play `pairs` game pairs.

MatchSummary.description: A match without its moves, for lists.

oneOf.description: A clock for each side: `seconds` for the game plus `increment` seconds after every move.
A fixed number of nodes per move. There is no clock.
A fixed time per move, in milliseconds. There is no clock.

name.description: Names the batch; list it with `?batch=`.

bounds.description: SPRT bounds in normalized Elo for `preset`, such as `[0, 3]`. Left out (and no `pairs`), `[0, 3]`.

hypothesis.description: What the change is expected to do, and why.

ltc.description: Add an LTC confirmation to the default funnel.

name.description: A short name. Defaults to the dev ref.

pairs.description: Play this many game pairs for `preset` instead of an SPRT.

oneOf.description: Shorthand for a single match with these settings, instead of a funnel.

stages.description: Run these stages instead of the default funnel for the kind.

oneOf.description: The standard start position.
A FEN (or `startpos`) with moves played from it, in UCI notation.
A random line of the opening book the tests use.

Pentanomial.description: Game-pair outcomes from the dev engine's side: `[LL, LD, WL+DD, WD, WW]`, i.e. pairs scoring 0, ½, 1, 1½ and 2.

build.description: The build that played, by id. Absent for a Lichess opponent, which is not one of ours.

commit.description: The first seven characters of its commit; empty for a Lichess opponent.

lichess.description: The Lichess username the player played under, ours included.

name.description: The ref the build was made from, such as `main`; for a Lichess opponent, its username.

rating.description: The Lichess rating the player had for this game's speed.

title.description: The Lichess title, such as `BOT` or `GM`.

Point.description: One point of a test's progress, for its chart.

Preset.description: Named settings, as Reckless names its tests.

Ratings.description: A bot's rating at each speed it has played.

reckless_dir.description: The Reckless checkout the runner builds from.

oneOf.description: Centipawns.
Mate in this many moves; negative when the side to move is mated.

mate.description: Mate in this many moves; negative when the side to move is mated.

Score.description: A search score from the side to move's point of view.

SeekChallenge.description: The challenge the bot has sent and is waiting on.

id.description: The challenge id, which becomes the game id if it is accepted.

SeekClock.description: A clock to challenge at: the initial time and the increment, in seconds.

SeekMode.description: Whether, and how, the bot is looking for games.

rating.description: Their rating at the challenge's speed.

mode.description:
`once` looks until one game starts; `always` looks again after every game, and across restarts, until stopped.
`off` stops, as `DELETE` does.

note.description: A short sentence on how the search last went, for people to read.

oneOf.description: The challenge sent and not answered yet. There is never more than one.

Settings.description: The bot's settings: what plays, how, and which challenges it accepts. Stored in the database.

build.description:
The build that plays: an id such as `12`, or a ref such as `main` meaning the newest build of it at the start of
each game. Nothing plays (challenges are declined) until one is chosen.

from_position.description: Also accept standard chess from a set position (Lichess's `fromPosition`). Other variants are always declined.

hash.description: Hash table size in MiB. Default 64.

max_games.description: Games at once. Challenges beyond this are declined as `later`. Default 1.

max_increment.description: The largest increment accepted, in seconds.

max_initial.description: The longest initial clock accepted, in seconds.

min_increment.description: The smallest increment accepted, in seconds.

min_initial.description: The shortest initial clock accepted, in seconds.

move_overhead.description:
Milliseconds the engine keeps in hand on every move for the network, as Reckless's `MoveOverhead` (0 to 2000).
Default 300.

seek_clocks.description:
The clocks the bot challenges other bots at when it looks for a game, as Lichess writes them: minutes plus
increment seconds, such as `3+2`. One is picked at random for each challenge. Default 3+0, 3+2 and 5+3.

seek_range.description:
The rating window for opponents when looking for a game: bots within this many points of ours at that speed
are preferred, then within twice as many, then any. Default 300.

seek_rated.description: Whether the challenges it sends when looking for a game are rated. Default true.

speeds.description: The speeds accepted. Correspondence is never played.

Speed.description: A Lichess speed the bot can play. Correspondence is not one.

Sprt.description: The SPRT a test runs: Elo bounds in normalized Elo, and the error rates.

oneOf.description: Bench both builds. A functional change must change the node count, and a non-functional one must not.
Bench both builds in turn, several times, and fail when dev is measurably slower.

allOf.description: A match between the builds; it passes when its SPRT accepts, or when its fixed games are played.

oneOf.description: A match between the builds; it passes when its SPRT accepts, or when its fixed games are played.

detail.description: One line on why, with the numbers.

test.description: The match, for a match stage.

points.description: Progress over the match: LLR and nElo by games played.

oneOf.description: Seconds per game plus an increment per move.

clock.description: Seconds per game plus an increment per move.

oneOf.description: A fixed number of nodes per move: no clock, so speed does not count, only search and evaluation.

nodes.description: A fixed number of nodes per move: no clock, so speed does not count, only search and evaluation.

TimeControl.description: How long each move may take.

token.description: A Lichess personal API token with the `bot:play` scope, made at https://lichess.org/account/oauth/token.

confirm.description: Must be `true`: the upgrade cannot be undone.
